findings.title: Two of this item's fixes are guarded by nothing — one cannot be guarded by a test, and the rule that would guard it was removed by this same change
findings.evidence:
Four faults were fixed on this branch. The rail accessible name has a test proven to fail without it, by removing the attribute and watching one of five cases fail. The other two have no guard at all.

First, use-media-query.ts. Five tests were written for it, then run against the old setState-in-effect implementation: all five pass. That is correct, because the refactor preserved behaviour by design, so no test should distinguish them — which means the shape it fixed can only be guarded by a lint rule. ESLint was then run over the old implementation on this branch and reported nothing, because this change replaced the react-hooks 7 recommended spread with one named rule and set-state-in-effect was not it. So the fix made by the change whose purpose is to end unguarded rules is itself unguarded.

Second, first-run.tsx's separation of the save's catch from the navigation. No test covers it, because react-router rejects a navigation only when a loader, an action or a blocker intervenes and this app configures none, so the path is unreachable without mocking the router into a state the product cannot reach.
findings.fix: ITEM-4 exists for the first and names it in its goal: enable react-hooks/set-state-in-effect, which also catches the quick-add fault it was pinned to avoid, and see it fail once on purpose before relying on it. For the second, add the test with the first route loader, action or blocker, which is when the path becomes reachable; until then the separation is held by reading and by the comment that states why the navigation sits outside the catch.

summary: Pass, with 1 medium finding open. No serious problem. FE-08 was the rule this branch was failing and now holds: a navigation that fails after a successful save no longer reports the owner's figures as lost. CODE-16 holds more closely than before, useSyncExternalStore being React's own hook for this. The finding is that two of the four fixes are guarded by nothing — one provably cannot be guarded by a test, and the lint rule that would guard it was removed by this same change. ITEM-4 closes it.
